verdict.rationale: Grok Build documents its own ACP mode, which runs Grok as an agent over JSON-RPC so it can be used inside other apps. That is a plausible route for in-editor chat, but the evidence never names an IDE, an extension, or an in-IDE chat experience. The 'IDE integration' mention in docs-5 refers to the grok-4.7 model on the xAI API, not to Grok Build, so it earns no credit here. missing for 10: a documented first-party IDE extension or named supported editors, evidence of chat inside the IDE with editor context (open file or selection), and independent hands-on corroboration of IDE use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can chat with the coding assistant directly inside my IDE for contextual help

citations.quote: This runs Grok as an ACP agent over JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout.
Use it via an interactive TUI, headlessly in scripts or bots, or through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) in other apps
